transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the final check for the 'Tidal Memory' installation plan in Gallery 4. Before I approve the public opening plan, I need to hear from each of you — rights, technical, accessibility, and artist representatives — on whether there are any conditions that must be added to the current draft. The plan as it stands proposes online-connected playback, eight visitor stations, 15-minute sessions, and a 5:00 PM public opening on October 12. Please share any conditions or concerns now.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical condition from the music license. I reviewed the countersigned license this morning — it just arrived after the exhibition packet was circulated. The license imposes three conditions: first, 'Tidal Memory' may be exhibited only through offline local playback, not online-connected playback; second, visitors may not photograph or record the installation; and third, the exact credit line 'Music licensed from Harborlight Editions' must be used. The current draft plan's proposal for online-connected playback is not permissible under the license, so that must be changed to offline local playback before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a critical technical condition to add. Yesterday after the installation rehearsal, I completed the headset and network test and found that the approved headset model supports only six simultaneous stations — not eight as proposed — and each session is limited to exactly 12 minutes to prevent thermal shutdown. The test report is still in the equipment vendor's queue, so it hasn't been formally circulated yet, but these are hard constraints. The current draft plan's proposal for eight stations and 15-minute sessions must be revised to six stations and 12-minute sessions before approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have an accessibility condition that must be added. I confirmed with the festival's access consultant today that one of the six stations must be a seated, step-free station, and that every visitor notice must display the exact warning 'Flashing light and sudden sound'. The consultant's written confirmation arrived after the draft visitor signage was already sent to print, so the signage will need to be corrected before approval. These are required conditions for the installation plan.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a condition from the artist's side. I confirmed with the artist's manager this afternoon that the artist will permit public access on October 12 only from 6:00 PM onward — not 5:00 PM as currently proposed — and will not permit press or invited photographers inside before that opening. The manager's email is awaiting entry in the artist file, but these are firm requirements. The public opening time in the draft plan must be changed from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM, and no press or invited photographers may be allowed inside before 6:00 PM on October 12.
